from time import * from physical import * from environment import Environment from ioeclient import IoEClient from gpio import * from pyjs import JsObject
# This will contain an object that specifies how the sensor should work. g_sensorData = None
# Callback for processing values g_processValue = lambda unprocessedValue, deviceIDS: None
# Callback for mouse events g_processMouse = lambda pressed, x, y, firstPress: None
# Used to determine mouse clicks. g_wasMouseClicked = False
# Checks for environment sound and sound in devices and combines the decibels. # A delay will run each update. It will be for this amount of time. # Setting to 0 means there is no delay. g_delayTime = -1
# Internal types for differentiating the search types. def environmentType(): return 'ENVIRONMENT'
def propertyType(): return 'PROPERTY'
# Internal type to differentiate the slot write types. def analogType(): return 'ANALOG'
def customType(): return 'CUSTOM'
def digitalType(): return 'DIGITAL'
# Purpose: # Set the wait time to check the environment again # timeMSec: >0 - wait in millisec, -1 - no wait, 0 - idle wait def setWaitTimeMSec(timeMSec): global g_delayTime g_delayTime = timeMSec
# Purpose: # Set the callback to process mouse events def setCallbackOnProcessMouse(callback): global g_processMouse g_processMouse = callback
# Purpose: # Set the callback to processe value def setCallbackOnProcessValue(callback): global g_processValue g_processValue = callback
# Purpose: # Set the callback to processed value access def setCallbackOnProcessValue(callback): global g_processValue g_processValue = callback
# Purpose: # Update the sensor. Send value as specified. def updateSensor(): if None is not g_sensorData: unprocessedValue = None value = None deviceIDS = []
# Handle an environment value sensor. if environmentType() is g_sensorData.type: unprocessedValue = Environment.get(g_sensorData.propertyName) elif propertyType() == g_sensorData.type: if None is not g_sensorData.searchData: if getattr(g_sensorData.searchData, "w", None) and getattr(g_sensorData.searchData, "h", None): # Search an area. x = getX() y = getY()
if 'CENTER' is g_sensorData.searchData.offset: x = getCenterX() y = getCenterY()
x -= (g_sensorData.searchData.w/2) y -= (g_sensorData.searchData.h/2) elif 'WORKSPACE' is g_sensorData.searchData.offset: x = 0 y = 0
# Search in a range around it. devices = devicesAt(x, y, g_sensorData.searchData.w, g_sensorData.searchData.h)
deviceProperty = None
unprocessedValue = [] for dev in devices: if g_sensorData.searchData.deviceIDs: for dev_id in g_sensorData.searchData.deviceIDs: deviceProperty = getDeviceProperty(dev, g_sensorData.propertyName) if (dev is dev_id) and deviceProperty: unprocessedValue.append(deviceProperty)
deviceIDS.append(dev) break else: deviceProperty = getDeviceProperty(dev, g_sensorData.propertyName) if deviceProperty: unprocessedValue.append(deviceProperty) deviceIDS.append(dev)
# If there was a value then handle it. if None is not unprocessedValue: value = g_processValue(unprocessedValue, deviceIDS)
# Send the signal. if None is not g_sensorData.signalData: if analogType() is g_sensorData.signalData.type: analogWrite(g_sensorData.signalData.slot, value) elif customType() is g_sensorData.signalData.type: customWrite(g_sensorData.signalData.slot, value) elif digitalType() is g_sensorData.signalData.type: digitalWrite(g_sensorData.signalData.slot, HIGH if value > 0 else LOW)
g_sensorData.lastKnownValue = unprocessedValue g_sensorData.lastProcessedValue = value
# If set to handle the registration server, update it. if g_sensorData.updateRegistrationServer: IoEClient.reportStates(g_sensorData.lastProcessedValue)
# If set to handle the registration server, update it. if g_sensorData.updateRegistrationServer: IoEClient.reportStates(g_sensorData.lastProcessedValue)
updateMouseClick()
setDeviceProperty(getName(), "state", g_sensorData.lastProcessedValue);
# Wait if specified. if g_delayTime > 0: delay(g_delayTime) elif g_delayTime == 0: sleep(0)
# Purpose: # Update mouse clicked state so the main loop would know whether the mouse was pressed at least once def mouseEvent(pressed, x, y, firstPress): global g_wasMouseClicked if firstPress: # we don't need the False branch for this if g_wasMouseClicked = firstPress if g_processMouse: g_processMouse(pressed, x, y, firstPress)
# Purpose: # Update mouse click detection and sets the internal flag to show if a click happened in the current update. def updateMouseClick(): global g_wasMouseClicked g_wasMouseClicked = False
# Purpose: # Return if the mouse was last in a click state. Value is true for click, false for not. # This is only true for the first press, it counts as the click. def getMouseClicked(): return g_wasMouseClicked
# Purpose: # Sets the object up to detect and environment variable. # propertyName - The environment variable to get. # signalData - Object that contains data for how to send a signal. Is it digital, analog, the slot. def setupDetectEnvironment(propertyName, signalData): global g_sensorData g_sensorData = JsObject({ "type": environmentType(), "propertyName": propertyName, "signalData": JsObject(signalData), "lastProcessedValue": None, # Store the last processed sensor value. "lastKnownValue": None, # Stores the last unprocessed sensor value. "updateRegistrationServer": False # True to auto handle registration server updating. })
# Purpose: # Sets the object up to detect a property in an script object. # propertyName - The property name to find. # searchRange - Object that contains information on how the search should be conducted. Just things in a range, specific names, etc. # signalData - Object that contains data for how to send a signal. Is it digital, analog, the slot. def setupDetectProperty(propertyName, searchData, signalData): global g_sensorData g_sensorData = JsObject({ "type": propertyType(), "propertyName": propertyName, "searchData": JsObject(searchData.__dict__), "signalData": JsObject(signalData), "lastProcessedValue": None, # Store the last processed sensor value. "lastKnownValue": None, # Stores the last unprocessed sensor value. "updateRegistrationServer": False # True to auto handle registration server updating. })
# Purpose: # Creates and returns an object with information on how to search for device properties. # deviceID - A single string. The string would be a device name that should have it's property checked. # If you don't want it restriced to specific devices, just pass null. # w, h - Search area dimensions. If you only want in a specific range around the sensor you would set the width and height. Don't pass # anything if the entire workspace should be searched. # offset - null or 'TOP_LEFT' if the top left corner is the starting point, # 'CENTER' if the search area should be around the center of the device. # 'WORKSPACE' if the entire workspace should be checked. w and h will be ignored. def createPropertySearch (deviceID, w, h, offset): if (None is w or None is h): w = 4000 h = 4000 offset = 'WORKSPACE'
search = JsObject({"deviceIDs": [], "w": w, "h": h, "offset": offset}) if (None is not deviceID): search.deviceIDs[0] = deviceID
return search
# Purpose: # Creates and returns an object with information on how to search for device properties. # deviceIDs - An array of strings. Each string would be a device name that should have it's property checked. # If you don't want it restriced to specific devices, just pass null. # w, h - Search area dimensions. If you only want in a specific range around the sensor you would set the width and height. Don't pass # anything if the entire workspace should be searched. # offset - null or 'TOP_LEFT' if the top left corner is the starting point, # 'CENTER' if the search area should be around the center of the device. # 'WORKSPACE' if the entire workspace should be checked. w and h will be ignored. def createPropertySearchDevices(deviceIDs, w, h, offset): if (w is None or h is None): w = 4000 h = 4000 offset= 'WORKSPACE'
search = JsObject({"deviceIDs": [], "w": w, "h": h, "offset": offset}) if None is not deviceIDs: search.deviceIDs = deviceIDs
return search
# Purpose: # Creats and object that defines writting to an analog slot. def createAnalogWrite (slot): return {"type": analogType(), "slot": slot}
# Purpose: # Creats and object that defines writting to an analog slot. def createCustomWrite(slot): return {"type": customType(), "slot": slot}
# Purpose: # Creats and object that defines writting to an digital slot. def createDigitalWrite(slot): return {"type": digitalType(), "slot": slot}
# Purpose: # Returns the last update value before it was processed. def getLastKnownValue(): return g_sensorData.lastKnownValue
# Purpose: # Returns the last update value after it was processed. def getLastProcessedValue(): return g_sensorData.lastProcessedValue
# Purpose: # Setup a generic registration server entry for the sensor based on the slot write type the sensor is setup to use. # If it is digital it will be true, false. # Analog would be strings. # Custom is not supported. # The property will be marked as not-controllable and will only output values. # sensorName, sensorProperty - The text that will be displayed in the registration server. def setupRegistrationServer(sensorName, propertyName): if None is not g_sensorData: g_sensorData.updateRegistrationServer = True
sensorType = None if analogType() is g_sensorData.signalData.type: sensorType = 'number' elif digitalType() is g_sensorData.signalData.type: sensorType = 'bool' else: g_sensorData.updateRegistrationServer = False print 'Slot type not applicable for registration'
if g_sensorData.updateRegistrationServer: IoEClient.setup({ 'type': sensorName, 'states': [{ 'name': propertyName, 'type': sensorType, 'controllable': False }] }) else: print 'Slot type not specified, cannot setup registration server'

These values match up with the value when finding groups of data (devices). It is ignored for # finding environment variables.
def processValue (value, deviceIDs): #print len(value) #print value # From the readings, determine what is the highest in detection reading in the correct range range and convert to be a strength [0, 255] maxInRange = 0 # var maxInRange outOfRange = False # var outOfRange
for ind in xrange(0, len(value)) : if int(value[ind]) > maxInRange: maxInRange = int(value[ind])
#print maxInRange, g_sensitivity.low, g_sensitivity.high # Convert the in range value to a digital signal. if (g_sensitivity.low <= maxInRange) and\ (g_sensitivity.high >= maxInRange): value = HIGH else: value = LOW

THING_MODEL.SPECIFICATIONS:
Fire Monitor
Detect IR in the range of fire.

Features:
  • Registration Server Compatible
  • Detects flames by checking for a property and finding if the "IR" property value is in the range the detector considers a fire and outputs a digital signal.
Usage:
  • Objects that can be on fire should have a device property "IR" with value.  The IR range that is detected as fire is specified in the script.  Anything near the detector end will be checked for fire and a digital signal of HIGH or LOW will be sent based on the current detection.  HIGH for fire, LOW for no fire detected
Direct Control:
  • N/A
Local Control:
  • N/A
Remote Control:
  • N/A
Data Specifications:
  • Message Format: [state]
    state: 0 = no fire, 1 = fire
  • Output Slot: D0
    LOW = no fire, High = fire
Example:
  • Create an Thing and in the script set a fire property with setDeviceProperty(getName(), 'IR', 900);
  • Connect the fire sensor to a LED that has been modified to check for a digital signal, and turn the LED on when the signal is not 0.
  • Move the detector near the fire to see the LED light up.
